text:
alex: Heads-up — Snyk flagged a public gist with something that looks like a Redwood SDK key. Pattern matches `rk_live_` and snippet includes `rk_live_9aG...`. Link: https://gist.github.com/??? :eyes:
security-bot: Automated detection: potential token leak detected for pattern 'rk_live_*'. Created alert ID: ALERT-8921.
maya: Thanks. Can someone confirm if the prefix matches our live keys or an old test key? Last 4 chars would help (we don't want to post full key here).
sam: I'm checking auth logs now. Quick grep showed inbound requests using that token from 3 IPs since 04:12 UTC hitting /v1/embeddings. Last 4 chars in logs: `...G7f3`.
alex: That aligns with the gist snippet (ends in G7f3). Not good.
oncall-ops: I'm starting containment: creating rotated key, will invalidate the exposed token and add IP blocks for the suspicious IPs. Will post commands and IDs when done.
sam: Running revoke: ```bash
# internal token service
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  https://tokens.internal.redwood/api/v1/revoke 
  -d '{"token_suffix":"G7f3"}'
```
oncall-ops: Revoke call returned 200. Response: ```json
{"status":"revoked","token_suffix":"G7f3","revoked_at":"2026-03-20T04:20:14Z"}
```
devex-bot: New token created for service: rk_live_2kL... (stored in Secrets Manager, not printed here). Secret version: sm://projects/redwood/secrets/sdk_keys/versions/78
carlos-cs: Quick check with CS systems — no customer tokens appear to have been shared. The requests were to our internal embeddings route from the exposed key, not customer API keys. No user IDs or PII seen in those requests' payloads per initial sampling.
lina-legal: Hold on notifications: we need to confirm data access and scope before any customer comms. If only service-to-service traffic and no customer data, we can avoid broad customer notice but document for compliance.
maya: Action list (short): 1) Revoke exposed token (done). 2) Rotate any sibling keys for that service. 3) Search public repos/gists and s3 buckets for the suffix/prefix. 4) Confirm no data exfiltration. 5) Add IPs to blocklist and create temporary WAF rule. 6) Update audit log retention window and snapshot logs. 7) Postmortem & prevent recurrence.
sam: I'm kicking off gitleaks across org repos + public scan: ```bash
gitleaks detect --source . --report-format json --pattern "rk_live_" --report-path /tmp/gitleaks.json
# also scanning s3 buckets via internal-scan tool
internal-scan s3 --pattern rk_live_ --output /tmp/s3scan.json
```
oncall-ops: WAF rule added and IP blocks in place. Throttled embed route to 5r/s for the service key family.
alex: Found one more occurrence in a forked repo that had been deleted yesterday; DevEx will PR a secrets-removal and update docs to remind devs to not paste keys in examples.
devex-bot: Created PR #4049 to remove leaked key references and added pre-commit hook update to enforce `gitleaks` scan at commit time for repos under /examples.
maya: Good. For long-term: add policy to rotate service keys every 90 days, integrate token issuance with KMS-backed envelope encryption and stricter RBAC. Also update CI to fail if any live key pattern is detected.
lina-legal: Please preserve all evidence and timestamps for potential regulatory follow-up. File incident with compliance case ID CASE-1172.
carlos-cs: No customer-facing incidents opened. If anything changes, I'll escalate.
alex: Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC. Owner: maya. Deliverables: timeline, root cause (how key got into gist), detection gaps, remediation, follow-up controls.
maya: I'll draft an internal incident note and share before the postmortem. Closing checklist: rotate sibling keys, confirm no exfiltration, update secrets scanning rules, document lessons.
oncall-ops: Incident ticket INC-4598 updated with steps and timeline. Marking thread resolved for now but keeping ticket open until postmortem action items complete. :white_check_mark:
